title: Novel Process for 3D Printing Decellularized Matrices
protocol: Add 7.5 mM sterile NaOH to adjust pH and achieve a concentration of 1.25 mg/ml.
Prepare fresh working solutions for injection 30 minutes before each time point.
Harvest cartilage plugs from porcine hind limbs.
Decellularize the cartilage with trypsin/EDTA, DMEM, peracetic acid/Triton X-100 in sequence.
Rinse decellularized matrix thoroughly and freeze it.
Lyophilize the frozen matrix, then grind and dissolve it in pepsin solution.
Dissolve PLA in dichloromethane and mix with the pepsin-dissolved matrix.
Add the mixture dropwise into a 3% polyvinyl alcohol aqueous solution.
Centrifuge the resultant microspheres, rinse them, drain excess liquid, and lyophilize again.
Sieve the prepared microspheres using cleaned sieve plates to ensure uniform size.
Place dry microspheres in the topmost sieve tray and place the lid on the top tray.
Turn on coarse sieving for 8 to 10 min.
Repeat on fine for 8 to 10 min.
Carefully remove the sieve plates one by one and place them upside down on a large weigh paper.
Tap the sides gently to ensure most of the spheres have fallen out onto the paper.
Discard oversized spheres (>106 µm) and undersized spheres (<53 µm).
Add spheres in the 53 to 106 µm size range to a labeled centrifuge tube with type and batch number.
Place the tube in a -20 °C freezer until further use.
Perform macroscopic/visual assessment to check that the microspheres are uniform, spherical, and have no aggregates.
Assess the microspheres using a scanning electron micrograph (SEM).
Place microspheres onto an SEM chuck and sputter coat with gold-palladium in argon atmosphere to a thickness of 4 nm.
Observe surface features, morphology, and diameters of the microspheres using a 10 kV accelerating voltage and a 10 mm working distance.
Measure and record the mass of the microspheres; at least 25 g is needed.
Add polycaprolactone (PCL) powder to the microspheres for a 1:4 weight ratio of microspheres to PCL.
Mix the powder mixture on a miniature rolling mixer at 20 rpm for 5 min.
Flip the container and mix at 20 rpm for an additional 5 min.
Remove the insulating material from the extruder if necessary.
Use desktop fans to cool the extruder and filament during production.
Setup the equipment setup for extrusion.
Position the extruder so that its outlet is ~60 cm from the inlet to the spooler, with a direct path from the extrusion outlet to the spooler inlet.
Raise the spooler 3-4 inches from the bench if necessary to prevent filament drooping.
Place a desktop fan ~15 cm from the heating jacket and direct it towards the heating jacket for cooling with ambient air throughout filament production.
Place a second cooling fan approximately halfway between the extruder and spooler and direct it towards the extrudate to assist in cooling the filament with ambient air.
Adjust the positioning as needed throughout the process.
Set the modified extruder heating element to 52 °C.
Turn on the desktop cooling fans.
Allow the instrument to come to equilibrium for 20 to 30 min.
Ensure that the proper nozzle is attached to the extruder.
Fill the extruder hopper with the microsphere/PCL mixture from step 3.3 just before beginning.
Turn on the spooler and the extruder auger to initiate extrusion of filament.
Manually pull the initial extrudate from the extrusion outlet with forceps and feed it to the filament spooler.
Monitor the process closely and modify parameters as necessary.
Adjust the extruder temperature, extrusion auger speed, and spooler speed to obtain a 1.75 mm diameter filament as measured by calipers.
Adjust the fans as needed to cool the filament properly to avoid non-circular filament cross-sections.
Mix and refill the hopper as necessary.
Continue extruding until all of the powder has been used and the hopper is almost empty.
Add PCL powder (without microspheres) to the hopper to flush out the microsphere mixture that is currently in the extruder.
Continue adding PCL powder to the hopper until no more microspheres are visible in the extrudate.
Label and separate the filament which contains the microspheres in the desired concentration.
Continue extruding until there is minimal powder left in the hopper.
Turn off the spooler, extruder auger, extruder heating element, and fans.
Design a geometry of the desired shape and form using computer aided design software.
Slice the model and dictate the toolpath using slicing software compatible with the 3D printing machine being used.
Load the filament from step 3 onto any standard FDM printer fitted with standard nozzles of the desired diameter (typically 0.4 mm).
Begin the print at 65-70 °C and 300 mm/min linear speed as the custom filament is deposited layer-by-layer by the machine.
Pay special attention to the first layer and adjust settings as needed to get a good quality print.
Print a geometry (n = 3) with an end mass of at least 400 mg using ALP microsphere filament (PLA-ALP/PCL).
Print PCL-only scaffolds of the same geometry as PLA-ALP/PCL scaffolds.
Submerge scaffolds in 1 mL Tris-HCl buffer.
Incubate for 24 h at 37 °C and 110 rpm rotation to allow enzyme diffusion.
Add 1 mL of 1 mg/mL p-nitrophenyl phosphate, disodium hexahydrate in Tris-HCl.
Incubate at 37 °C, 110 rpm for an additional 10 h.
Read the supernatant absorbance at 415 nm.
